steps.text: Combine the rice with the garlic in a large saucepan. Pour water and salsa into the rice mixture. Bring the water to a full boil and then reduce the temperature to simmer. Simmer for 20 minutes or until the rice is tender. Fluff the rice when finished.

raw_recipe.headline: Linnie's Spanish Rice
raw_recipe.description: The best and easiest Spanish rice!
raw_recipe.name: Linnie's Spanish Rice

recipeInstructions.text: Combine the rice with the garlic in a large saucepan. Pour water and salsa into the rice mixture. Bring the water to a full boil and then reduce the temperature to simmer. Simmer for 20 minutes or until the rice is tender. Fluff the rice when finished.

review.reviewBody: As per other reviewers, I sauteed the rice and garlic in a little butter. I also substituted chicken broth for the water and only added 3/4 of the jar of salsa. Turned out perfect! The whole family loved it!!! I did simmer covered, wasn't sure since it didn't say. I love simple recipes with so few ingredients that taste so flavorful! Will definitely make this again!!!!!!!

Good idea for a quick side dish but I agree with the last reviewer who said this had way to much salsa for 1 cup of rice. I suggest using 1/2 or 3/4 jar of salsa at most for each cup of uncooked rice. I may try again this way.

This was so simple and so good. I used Uncle Ben's rice in the microwave - no need for water and then added the salsa. I also added some sauteed chopped green pepper and onion along with some chili powder and cumin to give it a little something more.
Super easy & good! browned the rice like the others suggestion - made with La Victoria's thick & chunky medium salsa. Very tasty. I didn't cover it 'cause it didn't specify. Turned out great.

Made this Spanish Rice tonight! The family liked it very much. I did however make a few adjustments. First off, I used Jasmine Rice. I toasted the rice & garlic until golden brown with chopped onion in Olive Oil & added 3 Tablespoons of butter. I used Chicken Broth instead of water, ½ a 16oz jar of HEB Chunky Salsa. Boil on high until bubbly & simmered 20 minutes on low. Fluffed with spoon. Came out perfect! The Easiest Spanish Rice recipe ever!

Very bummed...I can never seem to get the right spanish rice recipe. This one seemed so easy and had great reviews, but I wasn't impressed. Way too much salsa; I used homemade which had the same consistency as the Pace brand, but it was too much. Maybe if I had used half or three quarters it would have been better.
This recipe was tasty and very simple. I used a garlic lime salsa and it had great flavor. I would make sure you use a salsa that has good flavor or your rice will be bland.

I had some leftover cooked taco filling I had to do something with. I also did not have any salsa. I used all the rice, some left over low Na vegetable broth and brought up the volume to 2 C, a 15 oz. can of petite diced tomatoes, about 1/4 C of green pepper chopped small, 1 tsp. minced garlic, and 2 tsp. of taco seasoning. We had it for dinner. It was really good but probably needed another teaspoon of taco seasoning. I threw this together when I was running out of time to figure out dinner without ordering takeout. Don’t be afraid to substitute!

It was OK but too much salsa. I use another recipe from this site which is delicious
2 TBSP oil
2 TBSP chopped onion
sauté lightly then add 1 1/2 cups rice, cook about 5 mins
Add 2 cups chicken stock and 1 cup salsa. Stir well and cook until rice is done. I add 1 pound of pre-cooked turkey sausage Oscar Meyer or similar) and mix well. With a salad and garlic bread I have a quick meal.

Using salsa to make the rice make this recipe sooo easy! I gave it 5 stars but didn’t follow exactly. Like others suggested I browned the garlic and rice in butter before adding any liquids, used bullion instead of water, and only used 1/2 the salsa called for. My boyfriend and I both agreed it came out perfect!

Simple, easy and definitely delicious! Cut this in half for just the 2 of us and then did saute my garlic and rice for a couple of minutes before adding my water and salsa! I think the salsa is key - it can make or break your rice depenidng on the flavour. I use a dried mix that you add your own fresh tomatoes and lime juice to and it's FANTASTIC!
I used a 10 oz. can of diced tomatoes and chilies instead of the salsa. I think that this would benefit from adding some salt before fluffing the rice.

I really like the ease of this recipe and think it has promise but I think the type of salsa used makes a huge difference! I used a homemade, runnier salsa and 1 c to the amount of rice? Too much and too salty. Served with Zucchini Enchiladas - which helped offset the saltiness. After having reviewed more reviews, may experiment again but with a low sodium, chunkier salsa. If Rice a Roni can do it?! Most certainly can I too! Glad we tried! Thanks Linda!

I have been making my Spanish rice for years, using salsa for the sauce. saves so much fuss. all the seasoning is in it. I do add burger and onion, and galic to kick it up. I bown the rice, burger and onion up and then add water to get the rice plumped and then the salsa . and simmer a bit more.

I thought this was the Spanish rice I usually make because it had salsa in it. It wasn’t. I prefer Best Spanish Rice because of the amount of salsa called for, the chicken broth instead of water, and the addition of onions. This one just isn’t as good.
Good for a hurry up dish. I'll probably add more the next time.

The first time I cooked the recipe, as written, and it was delicious and easy. I used Tostitos mild salsa. The second time I made the recipe it was bitter, however, I used a different salsa so be careful which salsa you use. I just made this recipe tonight, but this time I cooked up some ground beef and added it to the cooked rice. It was wonderful as a main dish. Thanks Linnie for sharing.
Super easy and you can determine the flavor/spiciness with your preffered/favorite salsa.

I gave it 4 stars as written, but read many reviews and made changes:crisp bacon, fresh tomatoes, chicken stock, 1/2 cup mild salsa and 1 cup tomato sauce, onion, black olives. We have to limit spicy foods, but this had so much flavor with changes. Oh, and I browned the rice in a little butter, with onion and garlic. Probably shouldn't review, having made so many changes, but reviewers' hints made all the difference for us. Thanks to all reviewers.

I guess I'm in the minority, but I used 3/4 c salsa and would have loved more! I found it a bit dry, but very quick and tasty. I will make this again with more salsa and maybe a bit of chili powder or cumin.
